answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a jade-tier stake that unlocks only after sustained useful work, like water slowly carving karst over time rather than appearing overnight. A new identity starts with zero reputation and earns trust gradually, while a raven-like observer network cross-checks work history, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real stake and time for each one, making a Sybil flood expensive and slow to rebuild after slashing.
